title: What is HELUT?
youtubeTitle: What is HELUT? — Homomorphic Edge Look-Up Tensors on Apple Silicon
description: A short intro to HELUT: Yosys netlists → Metal tensor datapaths, three research pillars (cleartext batch, torus FHE, TensorLUT), and what the project does — and does not — claim. Epoch C51. Site: https://helut.digitaldefiance.org · Source: https://github.com/Digital-Defiance/HELUT

scenes.headline: What is HELUT?
scenes.subhead: Homomorphic Edge Look-Up Tensors — a Metal datapath for circuit-shaped evaluation on Apple Silicon.
scenes.voiceover: HELUT stands for Homomorphic Edge Look-Up Tensors. It is a Swift and Metal systems prototype that turns Yosys gate-level netlists into a single Metal Performance Shaders Graph, and evaluates every look-up table as a dense tensor product on Apple Silicon.

scenes.headline: Not “Enigma only”
bullets: Enigma is one application of a general datapath
Combinational LUTs, sequential DFFs, batch parallelism
CPU-scale nets — PicoRV32 lw sees 1 (C50); Metal NOP-fetch (C51)
scenes.voiceover: The point is not Enigma only. Enigma is one application. The stack is a datapath for encrypted-shaped circuit evaluation: combinational look-up tables, sequential flip-flops, a batch axis for many machines at once, and a PicoRV32 RISC-V core that executes addi, store, and load under torus FHE. Claim C50 is an encrypted addi then store then load of one at demo N equals 8, about 79 milliseconds per tick on CPU. Claim C51 is the same core on Metal for a NOP fetch — two instruction addresses, about eight seconds per tick, tiled blind-rotate. Not a production-key CPU, and not Linux.

scenes.headline: Cleartext Metal · Torus FHE · TensorLUT
scenes.subhead: Same netlist substrate. Different jobs. Different claim bars.
scenes.voiceover: HELUT has three pillars that share the same netlist substrate. Pillar one is campaign-scale cleartext Metal — boolean-faithful batch search. Pillar two is graduated torus FHE — LWE and GLWE samples with blind-rotate per Yosys look-up table. Pillar three is TensorLUT — when the INIT tables themselves become the search space. Same silicon story. Different honesty bars.

scenes.headline: What actually runs today
bullets: Yosys JSON → MPSGraph compile and tick
Encrypted path with certificates and SING checks
Public claim sheet + reproduce commands — no lecture-voice invents
scenes.voiceover: What runs today is reproducible from the repo. Cleartext Metal evaluates Yosys look-up tables and flip-flops. The encrypted path encrypts those wires as lattice samples and blind-rotates per look-up table, with certificates for noise, hardness calibration, and measured bootstrap-key residual. Every public claim sits in a living claim sheet with a reproduce command. If it is not reproducible, we do not say it.

scenes.headline: What this is not
bullets: Not a decrypt of the live P1030680 campaign ciphertext
Estimator filled (C23) — H1: 4 of 8 anchors still exceed 16-bit merge tolerance
scenes.voiceover: Honesty matters as much as speed. HELUT is not a claim that we invented torus FHE. The P1030680 campaign path has not published a decrypt of that live ciphertext. The native Sage lattice-estimator cross-check is filled — claim C23. At the production row, HELUT quotes about 175.7 calibrated bits against the estimator's 180.2. The asterisk that stays printed is H1: four of the eight anchors still exceed the 16-bit merge tolerance, so do not quote 176 as estimator cost on every row. Discovery continues after any disclosure — the claim sheet moves when the evidence moves.

scenes.headline: Next: the Metal compiler
scenes.subhead: How Yosys gates become a single GPU graph.
scenes.voiceover: Next we open Pillar one: how a Yosys netlist becomes one Metal graph, and why the batch axis is the campaign engine. Source and reproduce commands live at helut.digitaldefiance.org and on GitHub under Digital Defiance.
